title: The Sixth Sense: The Door to the Temple of Wisdom
coreMove: Treat the sixth sense as disciplined receptivity: prepare the mind, rehearse judgment through chosen models, welcome hunches, and test them instead of obeying every impulse.

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder tempted to treat a good feeling as proof
exampleSpecs.stakes: a flattering offer could outrun the preparation that makes intuition trustworthy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the invisible counselors as trait rehearsal before giving authority to a hunch.

exampleSpecs.audience: a professional under pressure to confuse speed with courage
exampleSpecs.stakes: public action could satisfy anger while weakening judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show Abraham Lincoln as a counselor who gives moral judgment a concrete personality.

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations leader sorting signal from nerves
exampleSpecs.stakes: an odd warning could either reveal risk or distract from completed analysis
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat the Temple of Wisdom as a threshold reached after analysis, not a casual hunch.

exampleSpecs.audience: a director tempted to turn embarrassment into prophecy
exampleSpecs.stakes: one failed pitch could cancel useful work before it is tested
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the invisible counselors to convert admiration into standards after an emotional setback.

exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician deciding how to face a near miss
exampleSpecs.stakes: fear could disguise silence as prudence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Let Abraham Lincoln as counselor supply justice and resolve when fear distorts a hunch.

exampleSpecs.audience: a leader whose intuition may be defending pride
exampleSpecs.stakes: ceremonial certainty could bless a choice formed before reflection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the Temple of Wisdom as a prepared threshold that requires motive checking.
